title: grade-edge.json
description: One rung of a material grade ladder: a working that improves a thing by exactly one step. The anchor is `mt-turn-the-poor-ore`'s gloss, which specifies the whole mechanic in two sentences — "Change worthless rock into ore that is merely bad. Never into good ore: the working improves a thing by one step and has never once been made to take two." That is three grades (0 worthless / 1 worked / 2 fine), an ordinal on them, a converter that moves one step, and a cap on how far one working can move. `toGrade` must equal `fromGrade + 1`: the one-step rule is a schema-and-loader invariant, not a runtime convention, because a rung that skipped would be authorable and would read as content rather than as a defect. `ratio` below fp(1024) is a conversion that loses — `mh-the-second-harvest`'s "Nothing is created; a field of straw becomes a smaller field of grain" — and fp(1024) is a rung whose gloss states no loss. `inputPerTick` is what the rung draws from the grade below each world tick while its node is known; it is a claim on the stock adjudicated by CONSUMPTION_ORDER for grade 0, and against the graded stock above it. Every magnitude here is untuned (docs/design/release-plan.md): no release before 0.5.0 may claim any of them is balanced.

gradedKind.description: Which of the seven material kinds carries a ladder. Only `stone` does today, and the narrowness is deliberate: a graded stock with a producer and no consumer is a label on a resource, which docs/design/economy-flow-models.md §4 refuses. Widening this enum means authoring both ends and adding the columns `material-grade` carries.

grade.description: 0 worthless / 1 worked / 2 fine. Three, because two independent glosses converge on three — `mt-turn-the-poor-ore`'s worthless/bad/good and `maq-sweeten-the-cistern`'s foul/water/clean — and a fourth grade needs a gloss asking for it.
